name: What Hidden Conditions Can Change a Kitchen Remodeling Estimate?

mainEntity.name: Which hidden kitchen conditions should be discussed before comparing written remodeling estimates?
mainEntity.text: Which hidden kitchen conditions should be discussed before comparing written remodeling estimates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Written estimates often assume that walls, floors, wiring, plumbing, and framing are serviceable. Demolition can reveal water damage, leaking supply lines, deteriorated subfloors, mold, pest damage, ungrounded wiring, overloaded circuits, undersized ventilation, uneven walls, or structural changes that require additional work. Before comparing bids, ask each contractor what was inspected and what remains uncertain. Request photographs, moisture or electrical observations when relevant, and a written list of assumptions. Ask whether the estimate includes a contingency, what the contingency covers, and whether it is a contractor-controlled reserve or merely a budget recommendation. A contingency should not replace a clear change-order process. Confirm that corrective work requires written approval and that the contractor will provide a description, price, and schedule effect before proceeding when practical. Ask how urgent conditions that could cause damage are handled. Compare proposals by the quality of their assumptions, not just their contingency percentage. A bid that acknowledges uncertainty can be more reliable than a low bid that overlooks likely conditions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Potential hidden conditions include damaged subfloors, leaks, mold, outdated wiring, insufficient electrical capacity, uneven walls, plumbing problems, structural issues, and pest damage. Ask how each contractor will inspect, document, price, and approve corrective work if demolition reveals problems.
